name: sdm-tabular

reports.title: Swapping the head
reports.question: Holding Monroe's frozen embedding fixed, which in-context tabular model reads it best?
reports.takeaway: Kumo Tabular large is the best head, on top of all 45 combinations and at an eighth of TabFM's GPU time. But the head is the small lever: swapping it moves R² by a median 0.042, against 0.208 for the representation.
reports.summary: Every tabular foundation model in NVIDIA's structured-data-models package — TabICLv2, Kumo Tabular small, medium and large, and the 1.6-billion-parameter TabFM — reads the same frozen 720-d Monroe embedding on the same folds as Monroe + TabPFN 3, so the only thing that differs between arms is the head. The authors' own tabicl package, loading the same checkpoint as NVIDIA's TabICLv2 port, is the control.
reports.finding: Kumo Tabular large is on top of all 45 endpoint × metric combinations after Tukey's correction, the only arm never significantly worse than the best. In paired tests it is ahead of TabPFN 3 on 28 and behind on 6, and ahead of TabFM on 28 against 7 for an eighth of the GPU time. NVIDIA's TabICLv2 port reproduces upstream tabicl to within 0.008 R². Swapping heads moves R² by a median of 0.042 per endpoint, against 0.208 for the representation.
